#4723 -- are the depfile flags parsed under -P, and does exit 0 mean anything?

Generated by manual-cases.py. Commands are echoed exactly as they
were executed; exit statuses come from Python, not from
%ERRORLEVEL%, which a single cmd line expands at parse time and so
reports the previous command's status.

dxc: <repo>/build/Debug/bin/dxc.exe
version: dxcompiler.dll: 1.10(5433-ab540090)(1.9.0.5433) - 1.9.0.5433 (triage, ab5400907)

=== -MF is parsed in compile mode: an unwritable target is diagnosed
$ dxc -T ps_6_0 -E main -MF no-such-dir/dep.d repro.hlsl
exit=0x00000001
| 
| The system cannot find the path specified. no-such-dir/dep.d

=== the same -MF under -P: identical argument, no diagnostic at all
$ dxc -T ps_6_0 -E main -P -Fi parse-proof.i -MF no-such-dir/dep.d repro.hlsl
exit=0x00000000
| (no output)

=== control: an unknown /-style flag is accepted silently and exits 0
$ dxc -T ps_6_0 -E main -P -Fi parse-proof.i /ZZZNONSENSE repro.hlsl
exit=0x00000000
| (no output)

=== contrast: -Fo under -P IS diagnosed as ignored -- the list exists
$ dxc -T ps_6_0 -E main -P -Fi parse-proof.i -Fo parse-proof.dxo repro.hlsl
exit=0x00000000
| dxc warning : Warning: compiler options ignored with Preprocess.
| Warning: compiler options ignored with Preprocess.

=== the flags are real and documented: dxc -help
$ dxc -help
exit=0x00000000
(-help output, filtered to the flags in question)
|   -Fi <file>              Set preprocess output file name (with /P)
|   -MD        Write a file with .d extension that will contain the list of the compilation target dependencies.
|   -MF <file> Write the specified file that will contain the list of the compilation target dependencies.
|   -M         Dumps the list of the compilation target dependencies.
|   -Po                   Preprocess to file (deprecated, use /P /Fi instead)
|   -P                    Preprocess to file

READING

Case 1 vs case 2 is the whole point. The -MF argument is character
for character the same in both; only -P differs. Compile mode tries
to open the file and says so when it cannot. -P mode says nothing,
which means the option table accepted -MF and nothing downstream
ever asked for it. Case 3 shows why that silence cannot be read as
'-MF was rejected': dxc accepts /ZZZNONSENSE just as quietly, and
exits 0. Case 4 shows dxc already warns about OTHER output flags
that do nothing under -P (-Fo), so the silence for -M/-MD/-MF is an
omission from that list rather than a deliberate design.
